name: FL-23
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Lois Frankel holds an enormous financial edge: $2.3M raised and $1.2M on hand versus $163K for Deborah Adeimy
The district leans Democratic by about nine points
Prediction markets price Frankel's win odds at 95-97%
No public polls or expert ratings exist, and outside spending has been minimal
model.rationale: Frankel's incumbency, the district's Democratic lean, and a roughly fourteen-to-one fundraising advantage over Adeimy all point to a comfortable win, and prediction markets concur at 95-97 percent. With no polling contradicting the fundamentals, this stays in safe territory.
model.watch: A sharply Republican national environment, a late surge of outside spending against Frankel, or any fresh polling showing a much closer race would move this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lois Frankel, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this South Florida district, which leans Democratic by about nine points. She enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $2.3 million and holding more than $1.2 million on hand, while Republican challenger Deborah Adeimy has raised about $163,000. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Frankel and not at all against her.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the picture rests on the district's lean, incumbency, and fundraising, all of which favor Frankel. Prediction markets price her chances at roughly 95 to 97 percent, a strong but not absolute endorsement. The outlook is a comfortable Democratic margin, with meaningful uncertainty since Florida races have drawn little polling attention and late shifts remain possible.
